chunking: fixed-size character windows per page (no cross-page chunks)
metadata: document_id, source, page, chapter, section, section_title, page_type, char_start, char_end
vectorizer: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (local CPU, 384-d, L2-normalized; pgvector exact cosine)
hypothesis: Baseline. Fixed windows ignore sentence/paragraph boundaries, so evidence may be split across two chunks and chunks may start mid-sentence; expect the lowest Hit@1/Hit@3 and coherence.
notes: index A: 458 chunks, mean 467 chars / 96 tokens, 0 over 256-token limit; embed ~7.1s; cost $0. Gold page in top-3 for 14/15 dev and 5/5 test, but evidence split across chunks in 8 dev + 3 test questions. Dev misses: q02 q03 q04 q05 q07 q10 q11 q14 q15; test misses: q16 q18 q20. Coherence 0.80/2, grounding 1.40/2, filter compliance test 0/1. Hypothesis confirmed.

chunking: paragraph-aware: paragraphs rebuilt from line length (<110 chars = break), headings glued to next paragraph, grouped up to max size, oversized paragraphs split at sentence ends
hypothesis: Only chunking changes vs A. Keeping whole paragraphs should keep evidence and its conditions in one chunk; expect higher Hit@3 and coherence than A, at the cost of longer chunks with more mixed content.
notes: index B: 341 chunks, mean 572 chars / 116 tokens, 0 over 256-token limit; embed ~6.7s; cost $0. Dev misses: q02 q03 q15 (evidence split in 2 of them). Coherence 1.70/2, grounding 2.00/2, filter compliance dev 2/2, test 0/1 (q18 top-2 from ch1). Hypothesis confirmed.

chunking: same chunks as B (re-uses index B)
filter: chapter = value given with the question (assumed user input before retrieval); only for questions that have a filter, otherwise no filter
hypothesis: Only the filter changes vs B. For questions whose concept appears in several chapters (e.g. inflation in ch1 and ch3, shareholder in ch1 and ch2), restricting to the given chapter should remove wrong-chapter chunks and raise Hit@1; questions without a filter should score identically to B.
notes: Filter questions: q04 (ch1), q11 (ch2) dev; q18 (ch3) test. No extra ingest cost. Identical to B on dev (B already filter-compliant 2/2), so Hit@1 did not rise: hypothesis only partly confirmed. Test filter compliance 1/1 vs B 0/1 (q18), with no change in Hit. SELECTED: tie with B on all pre-set dev criteria (Hit@3, Hit@1, coherence, resources); chosen because it never scored worse and enforces the requested chapter scope.
